primaryIssues: Unknown Prisma connection pooling configuration in a serverless Next.js environment
No application-level or external cache layer detected (Redis/Memcached)
Possible connection pool exhaustion if Prisma not configured as a serverless-safe singleton or using an external pooler
No schema/index verification possible — unindexed hot-path queries may cause failures
No evidence of caching, pagination, or indexes for high-traffic reads — will not scale to 1M users
If payment flows (razorpay) do not use DB transactions, financial integrity risk at scale

findings.title: Serverless Next.js with Prisma — pooling configuration not verified
findings.detail: Dependencies include prisma, @prisma/client and @prisma/extension-accelerate, and auth lib @clerk/nextjs indicates a Next.js app. I could not access repository files (getRepoTree failed) to verify Prisma client instantiation or singleton pattern. In serverless environments, per-request PrismaClient instantiation can exhaust DB connections. No evidence of external pooler configuration in code search.

sources: searchCode results showing no PrismaClient usage or connection files
getRepoTree returned 'Repository or branch not found'

findings.breaksAt: Connection exhaustion risk around 50-200 concurrent DB connections depending on host limits; likely to surface under hundreds of concurrent requests if misconfigured
findings.fix: Instantiate PrismaClient as a singleton in serverless (attach to globalThis). Alternatively, configure an external pooler (Neon, PgBouncer) or ensure @prisma/extension-accelerate is correctly initialized. Add connection timeouts and health checks; run load tests.

findings.title: Prisma schema (schema.prisma) not found — cannot verify indexes or FK definitions
findings.detail: Code search for 'schema.prisma' returned no results and repository tree retrieval failed, preventing schema analysis. Without schema access, I cannot confirm whether hot-path filters or FK columns are indexed (e.g., product.slug, order.userId). This prevents validation of unbounded queries or missing FK indexes.

sources: getRepoTree failed so schema files could not be enumerated

findings.breaksAt: Unindexed queries on high-traffic endpoints will degrade performance at tens of thousands of users and become critical at 100k+ users
findings.fix: Provide prisma/schema.prisma or equivalent ORM schema files. Ensure indexes on frequently filtered columns and FK columns. Add explicit indexes and consider composite indexes for common multi-column filters.

findings.title: No cache layer detected in dependencies
findings.detail: Dependency scan did not reveal Redis, ioredis, connect-redis, or memcached packages. No repository files were accessible to confirm presence of hosted cache. Without caching, read-heavy endpoints will increase DB load; pagination and indexes become more critical.

sources: getDependencies output contains no Redis/Memcached packages
searchCode returned no .env.example or cache configuration files

findings.breaksAt: Sustained high read traffic (10k+ active users) leading to high DB QPS and latency
findings.fix: Introduce a cache layer (Redis) for expensive reads and session storage. Use CDN/HTTP caching for static and semi-static responses and implement cache invalidation for writes.

summary.topConcern: Unverified Prisma connection pooling in serverless Next.js environment — potential DB connection exhaustion
summary.estimatedScaleCeiling: Conservative safe ceiling ~500 concurrent users without verified pooling; expect failures beyond ~1k concurrent users if Prisma instantiated per-request
